name: Balanced Stone Heaps
description: There are $$$n$$$ heaps of stone. The $$$i$$$-th heap has $$$h_i$$$ stones. You want to change the number of stones in the heap by performing the following process once: You go through the heaps from the $$$3$$$-rd heap to the $$$n$$$-th heap, in this order. Let $$$i$$$ be the number of the current heap. You can choose a number $$$d$$$ ($$$0 \le 3 \cdot d \le h_i$$$), move $$$d$$$ stones from the $$$i$$$-th heap to the $$$(i - 1)$$$-th heap, and $$$2 \cdot d$$$ stones from the $$$i$$$-th heap to the $$$(i - 2)$$$-th heap. So after that $$$h_i$$$ is decreased by $$$3 \cdot d$$$, $$$h_{i - 1}$$$ is increased by $$$d$$$, and $$$h_{i - 2}$$$ is increased by $$$2 \cdot d$$$. You can choose different or same $$$d$$$ for different operations. Some heaps may become empty, but they still count as heaps. What is the maximum number of stones in the smallest heap after the process?
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$). Description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second lines of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$h_1, h_2, h_3, \ldots, h_n$$$ ($$$1 \le h_i \le 10^9$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the maximum number of stones that the smallest heap can contain.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1623C — Balanced Stone Heaps [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
